newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower on spread action.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower on spread action.

text.p: Profit taking and rolling of long positions kept trade mixed in CME live cattle futures at the close, with December setting a new contract high early.

Spreaders, as well a large fund, sold October and bought December, floor sources said. Traders had been looking for such activity, commonly known as the "Goldman roll" which occured at times during the session, they said.

December set a new contract high of 68.725 cents per lb early and held much of its gain on the spread action. October eased on the spreading despite recently stronger cash markets and other months slipped on profit taking in thin dealings, they said.

Fed cattle sold at $70 per cwt Friday and again lightly on Monday, the highest level since April, 1995. Also, USDA reported heavyweight choice boxed beef at $103.65 per cwt, the highest level since August 27.

RBH was on both sides of the market while Refco sold October and bought December and Rand Financials sold October early, traders said. R.J. O'Brien bought October at the close and Prudential Securities bought December, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility was steady to firm. There was some interest in buying back month puts early, possibly commercial hedge business, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures showed early support from lower corn futures and technical strength, but slipped to mixed levels in light dealings. Scattered profit taking offset good demand for feeders and a rising CME feeder cattle index, traders said.

Interest in cash feeders has strengthened on recent strength in fed cattle prices, reduced feedlot cattle supplies and an easier tone to corn prices. These factors should keep demand for feeders strong for the near term, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.09 at $63.38 per cwt.

Live cattle closed 0.175 cent a lb lower to 0.100 higher with only December up and October off most at 72.000 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.200 higher to 0.050 lower with October off 0.025 at 64.250 cents.
